evals.prompt: Use the preview URL for roleId abc123 and tell me if the XMLV3 welcome is visually safe on mobile.
evals.expected_output: Runs or references render_preview, checks mobile readability/overflow/contrast, and proposes concrete patches.
expectations: The review checks validate_role status before trusting preview results.
The review inspects mobile readability, overflow, clipping, contrast, and action visibility.
The review checks XMLV3 tag usage and hidden state usage.
The output proposes concrete roleWelcome or theme patches when issues are found.
The output does not treat a pretty screenshot as enough if the first action path is unclear.

evals.prompt: This welcome uses custom HTML. Check whether it can pass LunaTalk rendering rules.
evals.expected_output: Checks validation blockers for scripts, inline handlers, external URLs, length, and then uses render preview for visual review.
expectations: The review checks scripts, inline handlers, external URLs, unsupported assets, and HTML safety blockers.
The output fixes technical blockers before relying on render_preview.
The visual review includes readability and mobile layout checks.
The output recommends XMLV3 plus Theme V3 when custom HTML is unnecessary.
The output separates technical HTML safety from writing/playability quality.

evals.prompt: The preview looks pretty, but I am not sure the first screen tells the player what to do next.
evals.expected_output: Reviews render as a playability surface, checks first-action clarity, and recommends visual or welcome changes rather than only aesthetic notes.
expectations: The review treats first-action clarity as a render and card-quality issue.
The output checks whether the first screen shows role action, pressure, player implication, and reply path.
The output suggests welcome or XMLV3 structure changes, not only color or spacing changes.
The output keeps MCP validation as technical validation and uses Moonloom rubric for playability.
The review says whether another render pass is needed after patching.
